peers.name: CG POWER AND IND SOL LTD

bull_bear.body: BHEL's strong research and development capabilities and strategic partnerships may provide a competitive edge
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Diversified pan-India manufacturing footprint of 16 manufacturing units and 2 repair units across power, transportation, defence, aerospace, oil & gas and process industries
- Long operating history since 1964 with an extensive installed base of ~214 GW of power generating equipment in India and abroad, plus 6 major HVDC projects executed including a multi-terminal UHVDC project
- Government of India ownership (58.17% stake) supporting a strong position in the domestic capital goods / infrastructure sector
- Substantial and consistent R&D investment (~2.4% of revenue), 4 Research Institutes, 13 Centres of Excellence, 400+ patents and copyrights filed, 6,000+ total IPR capital, plus strategic alliances with global OEMs for technology access
- Global footprint across 94 countries with 14+ GW of power generation capacity delivered outside India
- All-time high order book (Rs 2,39,057 Crore as on 31 March 2026) providing revenue visibility, with active diversification into non-thermal segments (coal gasification, rail signalling, defence/aerospace, transmission, nuclear/SMR) reducing dependence on conventional thermal power
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Uncompensated contingent exposure to a single JV counterparty via corporate guarantee — The Corporate Guarantee issued by BHEL in FY 2024-25 on behalf of its joint venture, Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Limited, without charging any fee/consideration, continues to remain in force and has been recognised as a deemed investment with a corresponding financial liability under Ind AS 109 — an unremunerated contingent exposure concentrated in a single JV.
- Working-capital funding reliant on short-term borrowing instruments — For meeting short-term operational and working capital requirements, the Company continues to utilize various borrowing instruments such as Working Capital Demand Loans (WCDLs), loans against Fixed Deposits and listed Commercial Papers, exposing it to short-term refinancing and interest-rate conditions rather than long-term stable funding.
- Long execution, billing and collection cycle typical of large capital-goods/EPC projects — Trade Receivables stood at 100 days of Revenue from Operations and Trade Payables at 165 days of procurement in FY 2025-26 (though improved from 115 and 201 days respectively in FY 2024-25), reflecting the extended execution and collection cycles inherent to large government/PSU capital projects that require sustained, structured receivables monitoring to avoid liquidity strain.
- Order inflow and order book mix vary materially by segment and year — Order receipts and the outstanding order book for the Power Sector versus the Industry Sector (including export orders) fluctuated materially across FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26, indicating that revenue visibility is sensitive to the timing and mix of large project awards rather than a steady-state order flow.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), incorporated in 1964 as a Public Sector Undertaking, combines world-class engineering, manufacturing, project execution and after-sales support to serve the power (thermal, hydro, gas, nuclear, solar), transmission, transportation, defence, aerospace, oil & gas and process industries sectors. It operates through a 16-unit pan-India manufacturing network plus 2 repair units, serving Government, Government ministries, Government-owned entities, CPSEs, State PSUs, State electricity boards, Independent Power Producers and private companies as customers. BHEL is diversifying beyond its core thermal power business into coal gasification, rail signalling, nuclear/SMR and transmission (HVDC) to reduce dependence on conventional thermal power.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Power Generation Equipment:** Steam/utility boilers, Turbines and generators (thermal, hydro, gas, nuclear), Captive power plant equipment
- **Transmission:** HVDC systems and terminal stations, Power/distribution transformers, Substations/switchyards (GIS), Electricity distribution and control apparatus
- **Transportation:** Locomotives, Vande Bharat trainsets, Kavach rail signalling system
- **Defence & Aerospace:** Super Rapid Gun Mount (SRGM), Ceramic Radar Domes, Compact Heat Exchangers, Liquid Cooling Systems and Pump Modules for aerospace applications
- **Oil & Gas:** Compressors, Oil drilling rigs, Well heads and Christmas Tree valves, Sulphur Recovery Unit packages
- **Industrial Products:** Electric motors, Industrial valves
- **Coal-to-Chemicals:** Ammonium nitrate / coal gasification plant packages (LSTK)
- **Solar:** Solar Business Division products
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- BHEL-GE Gas Turbine Services Pvt. Ltd. (BGGTS) — JV: Joint venture, jointly controlled entity providing gas turbine services; BHEL holding 50% minus one share (~49.99%).
- NTPC-BHEL Power Projects Pvt. Ltd. (NBPPL) — JV: Joint venture with NTPC for power projects; BHEL holding 50%.
- Raichur Power Corporation Ltd. (RPCL) — JV: Jointly controlled entity; BHEL holding 22.14% (including shares held via nominee).
- Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Ltd. (BCGCL) — JV: Joint venture with Coal India Ltd (BHEL 49%, CIL 51%) for coal gasification; BHEL is a related-party counterparty supplying goods & services (Supply, Erection and Civil Services) for the Coal Gasification & Raw Syngas Cleaning Project (LSTK-1, 42 months from 08.01.2026) and the Syngas Purification Project (LSTK-2, 42 months from 10.02.2026).
- M/s Powerplant Performance Improvement Private Ltd. — associate: Dissolved during FY 2025-26 and accordingly no longer considered in consolidation.
- Employee benefit trusts (Provident Fund Trusts, Gratuity Trust, PRMB Trust, Pension Trust) — related party: Post-employment benefit plans of the Company, classified as other related parties under Ind AS 24.
- Central Government controlled entities (other PSUs, State-owned utilities, Railways, etc.) — related party: BHEL is a Central PSU under the administrative control of the Ministry of Heavy Industries; significant transactions occur with other Government-controlled entities on normal, market-driven, arm's-length terms.

outlook.body: Outlook: Stable; Strategy: Focus on energy transition and infrastructure development
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: Expansion into new markets and products
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strategically diversifying into new-growth, non-thermal sectors (transmission, rail transportation, coal gasification, defence & aerospace, industrial products, international business) to drive sustainable growth, enhance profitability and reduce dependence on the conventional thermal power business.
- Continuing to pursue suitable technology, supply, indigenisation and capability-building arrangements in identified growth areas to support a long-term diversification strategy.
- Adopting advance manufacturing initiatives, calibrated outsourcing and targeted capacity augmentation to align manufacturing capabilities with project requirements, reduce lead times and improve execution efficiency.
- Pursuing operational excellence and cost leadership via aggregation of procurement through centralised procurement and subcontracting, and continuous optimisation of manufacturing capacities.
- Structured, system-driven monitoring of receivables across projects and business segments to enhance collection efficiency and reduce dependence on short-term external borrowings.
- Positioning to capitalise on nuclear energy growth, including active support for development of Bharat Small Modular Reactors and other emerging nuclear technologies.
- Pursuing the pumped storage projects opportunity to support grid-balancing needs created by growing renewable energy penetration.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 the Company incurred Rs 671 Crore (Rs 536 Crore in the previous year) towards capital expenditure on modernization and rationalization of existing facilities, focused on enhancing operational efficiency, supporting productivity and aligning operations with evolving business needs, met primarily through internal accruals. To reinforce execution, the Company adopted advance manufacturing initiatives, calibrated outsourcing and targeted capacity augmentation to align manufacturing capabilities with project requirements and reduce lead times. BHEL made a strategic foray into the coal gasification sector through the coal-to-2,000 TPD Ammonium Nitrate project executed via its JV Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Ltd (LSTK1 package for Coal Gasification & Raw Syngas Cleaning Plant and LSTK2 package for Syngas Purification Plant). Two HVDC terminal station orders are under implementation to support long-distance transmission of renewable power to load centres. Manufacturing of 80 Vande Bharat trainsets is underway for Indian Railways. The Company expanded captive solar capacity to about 43 MWp, generating about 44 million units of electricity, up about 12% year-on-year, as part of its green manufacturing footprint (four additional manufacturing units assessed for GreenCo certification during the year, taking the total to twelve units certified over the last three years). Effective April 1, 2026 (post year-end), the Central Foundry Forge Plant was merged with the Heavy Electrical Equipment Plant and the Project Engineering & Systems Division was merged with the Heavy Power Equipment Plant, as part of organisational consolidation.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Renewed emphasis on energy security following recent geopolitical disruptions has reinforced the role of coal-based generation in national planning, with policy makers envisaging thermal capacity of 315 GW by 2035-36, enabling robust thermal power ordering.
- Growing penetration of renewable energy is creating a strong need for grid-balancing solutions, which the Government's roadmap for 100 GW of Pumped Storage Projects by 2035-36 is expected to address, opening a growth avenue for BHEL.
- Nuclear energy is set to play a pivotal role in India's energy security and decarbonisation journey; SHANTI Act reforms are expected to support the sector's growth towards the national objective of 100 GW nuclear power capacity by 2047.
- Transmission infrastructure is expected to play a crucial role in reliable integration of renewable energy into the grid; two HVDC terminal station orders under implementation position BHEL to support long-distance transmission of renewable power to load centres.
- The Government of India's Rs 37,500 Crore coal and lignite gasification initiative is expected to support the emerging coal gasification sector as a substantial growth opportunity for the Company.
- The combined benefits of improved working capital management, lower financing costs and enhanced execution support are expected to create a virtuous cycle of faster project execution, improved cash generation and higher profitability.
- Order inflow of Rs 75,916 Crore during FY 2025-26 (including export orders of Rs 209 Crore) took the outstanding order book to an all-time high of Rs 2,39,057 Crore as on 31 March 2026, providing healthy revenue visibility and a robust foundation for future business growth.
- Diversified and growth businesses (transmission, rail transportation, coal gasification, defence, industrial products and international business) contributed about 29% of FY 2025-26 order inflow, with a similar share expected in the outstanding order book carried forward into FY 2026-27.
- Non-thermal orders account for over Rs 66,000 Crore of the Rs 2,39,057 Crore outstanding order book, spanning Hydro and Nuclear Power, Coal-to-Chemicals, Rail Transportation, Defence and Aerospace, Power Transmission, Oil & Gas, Industrial Products and renewable energy businesses.
- Power Sector secured orders worth Rs 59,256 Crore in FY 2025-26, including Rs 8,288 Crore from the coal gasification segment and thermal orders of about 10 GW; Industry Sector and International Operations booked orders worth Rs 16,660 Crore, around 50% higher than the previous year, including a major +/-800 kV, 6,000 MW HVDC order for the Bhadla-Fatehpur link.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: BHEL's credit rating has been upgraded to CARE AA with a stable outlook, reflecting its improved operational and financial performance, with a strong order book and growth optionality in the power and industrial segments. The company's diversified product portfolio and strategic initiatives are expected to drive growth. However, risks such as intense competition and regulatory changes may impact its margins and profitability.

risks.risk: Uncompensated contingent exposure to a single JV counterparty via corporate guarantee
risks.note: The Corporate Guarantee issued by BHEL in FY 2024-25 on behalf of its joint venture, Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Limited, without charging any fee/consideration, continues to remain in force and has been recognised as a deemed investment with a corresponding financial liability under Ind AS 109 — an unremunerated contingent exposure concentrated in a single JV.

risks.risk: Working-capital funding reliant on short-term borrowing instruments
risks.note: For meeting short-term operational and working capital requirements, the Company continues to utilize various borrowing instruments such as Working Capital Demand Loans (WCDLs), loans against Fixed Deposits and listed Commercial Papers, exposing it to short-term refinancing and interest-rate conditions rather than long-term stable funding.

risks.risk: Long execution, billing and collection cycle typical of large capital-goods/EPC projects
risks.note: Trade Receivables stood at 100 days of Revenue from Operations and Trade Payables at 165 days of procurement in FY 2025-26 (though improved from 115 and 201 days respectively in FY 2024-25), reflecting the extended execution and collection cycles inherent to large government/PSU capital projects that require sustained, structured receivables monitoring to avoid liquidity strain.

risks.risk: Order inflow and order book mix vary materially by segment and year
risks.note: Order receipts and the outstanding order book for the Power Sector versus the Industry Sector (including export orders) fluctuated materially across FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26, indicating that revenue visibility is sensitive to the timing and mix of large project awards rather than a steady-state order flow.

one-line thesis: BHEL's credit rating has been upgraded to CARE AA with a stable outlook, reflecting its improved operational and financial performance, with a strong order book and growth optionality in the power and industrial segments. The company's diversified product portfolio and strategic initiatives are expected to drive growth. However, risks such as intense competition and regulatory changes may impact its margins and profitability.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: BHEL is India's leading state-owned (Government of India, 58.17% stake) engineering and manufacturing enterprise in the capital goods sector, designing, engineering, manufacturing and supplying power and industrial equipment for the power, transportation, defence, aerospace, oil & gas and process …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), incorporated in 1964 as a Public Sector Undertaking, combines world-class engineering, manufacturing, project execution and after-sales support to serve the power (thermal, hydro, gas, nuclear, solar), transmission, transportation, defence, aerospace, oil & gas and process industries sectors. It operates through a 16-unit pan-India manufacturing network plus 2 repair units, serving Government, Government ministries, Government-owned entities, CPSEs, State PSUs, State electricity boards, Independent Power Producers and private companies as customers. BHEL is diversifying beyond its core thermal power business into coal gasification, rail signalling, nuclear/SMR and transmission (HVDC) to reduce dependence on conventional thermal power.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- BHEL-GE Gas Turbine Services Pvt. Ltd. (BGGTS) — JV: Joint venture, jointly controlled entity providing gas turbine services; BHEL holding 50% minus one share (~49.99%).
- NTPC-BHEL Power Projects Pvt. Ltd. (NBPPL) — JV: Joint venture with NTPC for power projects; BHEL holding 50%.
- Raichur Power Corporation Ltd. (RPCL) — JV: Jointly controlled entity; BHEL holding 22.14% (including shares held via nominee).
- Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Ltd. (BCGCL) — JV: Joint venture with Coal India Ltd (BHEL 49%, CIL 51%) for coal gasification; BHEL is a related-party counterparty supplying goods & services (Supply, Erection and Civil Services) for the Coal Gasification & Raw Syngas Cleaning Project (LSTK-1, 42 months from 08.01.2026) and the Syngas Purification Project (LSTK-2, 42 months from 10.02.2026).
- M/s Powerplant Performance Improvement Private Ltd. — associate: Dissolved during FY 2025-26 and accordingly no longer considered in consolidation.
- Employee benefit trusts (Provident Fund Trusts, Gratuity Trust, PRMB Trust, Pension Trust) — related party: Post-employment benefit plans of the Company, classified as other related parties under Ind AS 24.
- Central Government controlled entities (other PSUs, State-owned utilities, Railways, etc.) — related party: BHEL is a Central PSU under the administrative control of the Ministry of Heavy Industries; significant transactions occur with other Government-controlled entities on normal, market-driven, arm's-length terms.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Power Generation Equipment:** Steam/utility boilers, Turbines and generators (thermal, hydro, gas, nuclear), Captive power plant equipment
- **Transmission:** HVDC systems and terminal stations, Power/distribution transformers, Substations/switchyards (GIS), Electricity distribution and control apparatus
- **Transportation:** Locomotives, Vande Bharat trainsets, Kavach rail signalling system
- **Defence & Aerospace:** Super Rapid Gun Mount (SRGM), Ceramic Radar Domes, Compact Heat Exchangers, Liquid Cooling Systems and Pump Modules for aerospace applications
- **Oil & Gas:** Compressors, Oil drilling rigs, Well heads and Christmas Tree valves, Sulphur Recovery Unit packages
- **Industrial Products:** Electric motors, Industrial valves
- **Coal-to-Chemicals:** Ammonium nitrate / coal gasification plant packages (LSTK)
- **Solar:** Solar Business Division products

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Renewed emphasis on energy security following recent geopolitical disruptions has reinforced the role of coal-based generation in national planning, with policy makers envisaging thermal capacity of 315 GW by 2035-36, enabling robust thermal power ordering.
- Growing penetration of renewable energy is creating a strong need for grid-balancing solutions, which the Government's roadmap for 100 GW of Pumped Storage Projects by 2035-36 is expected to address, opening a growth avenue for BHEL.
- Nuclear energy is set to play a pivotal role in India's energy security and decarbonisation journey; SHANTI Act reforms are expected to support the sector's growth towards the national objective of 100 GW nuclear power capacity by 2047.
- Transmission infrastructure is expected to play a crucial role in reliable integration of renewable energy into the grid; two HVDC terminal station orders under implementation position BHEL to support long-distance transmission of renewable power to load centres.
- The Government of India's Rs 37,500 Crore coal and lignite gasification initiative is expected to support the emerging coal gasification sector as a substantial growth opportunity for the Company.
- The combined benefits of improved working capital management, lower financing costs and enhanced execution support are expected to create a virtuous cycle of faster project execution, improved cash generation and higher profitability.
- Order inflow of Rs 75,916 Crore during FY 2025-26 (including export orders of Rs 209 Crore) took the outstanding order book to an all-time high of Rs 2,39,057 Crore as on 31 March 2026, providing healthy revenue visibility and a robust foundation for future business growth.
- Diversified and growth businesses (transmission, rail transportation, coal gasification, defence, industrial products and international business) contributed about 29% of FY 2025-26 order inflow, with a similar share expected in the outstanding order book carried forward into FY 2026-27.
- Non-thermal orders account for over Rs 66,000 Crore of the Rs 2,39,057 Crore outstanding order book, spanning Hydro and Nuclear Power, Coal-to-Chemicals, Rail Transportation, Defence and Aerospace, Power Transmission, Oil & Gas, Industrial Products and renewable energy businesses.
- Power Sector secured orders worth Rs 59,256 Crore in FY 2025-26, including Rs 8,288 Crore from the coal gasification segment and thermal orders of about 10 GW; Industry Sector and International Operations booked orders worth Rs 16,660 Crore, around 50% higher than the previous year, including a major +/-800 kV, 6,000 MW HVDC order for the Bhadla-Fatehpur link.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025-26 the Company incurred Rs 671 Crore (Rs 536 Crore in the previous year) towards capital expenditure on modernization and rationalization of existing facilities, focused on enhancing operational efficiency, supporting productivity and aligning operations with evolving business needs, met primarily through internal accruals. To reinforce execution, the Company adopted advance manufacturing initiatives, calibrated outsourcing and targeted capacity augmentation to align manufacturing capabilities with project requirements and reduce lead times. BHEL made a strategic foray into the coal gasification sector through the coal-to-2,000 TPD Ammonium Nitrate project executed via its JV Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Ltd (LSTK1 package for Coal Gasification & Raw Syngas Cleaning Plant and LSTK2 package for Syngas Purification Plant). Two HVDC terminal station orders are under implementation to support long-distance transmission of renewable power to load centres. Manufacturing of 80 Vande Bharat trainsets is underway for Indian Railways. The Company expanded captive solar capacity to about 43 MWp, generating about 44 million units of electricity, up about 12% year-on-year, as part of its green manufacturing footprint (four additional manufacturing units assessed for GreenCo certification during the year, taking the total to twelve units certified over the last three years). Effective April 1, 2026 (post year-end), the Central Foundry Forge Plant was merged with the Heavy Electrical Equipment Plant and the Project Engineering & Systems Division was merged with the Heavy Power Equipment Plant, as part of organisational consolidation.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified pan-India manufacturing footprint of 16 manufacturing units and 2 repair units across power, transportation, defence, aerospace, oil & gas and process industries
- Long operating history since 1964 with an extensive installed base of ~214 GW of power generating equipment in India and abroad, plus 6 major HVDC projects executed including a multi-terminal UHVDC project
- Government of India ownership (58.17% stake) supporting a strong position in the domestic capital goods / infrastructure sector
- Substantial and consistent R&D investment (~2.4% of revenue), 4 Research Institutes, 13 Centres of Excellence, 400+ patents and copyrights filed, 6,000+ total IPR capital, plus strategic alliances with global OEMs for technology access
- Global footprint across 94 countries with 14+ GW of power generation capacity delivered outside India
- All-time high order book (Rs 2,39,057 Crore as on 31 March 2026) providing revenue visibility, with active diversification into non-thermal segments (coal gasification, rail signalling, defence/aerospace, transmission, nuclear/SMR) reducing dependence on conventional thermal power
